# QUEUE — closed rows, moved by the archiver

**Written only by `node tools/ledger.mjs archive <ID>`**, which moves a closed row (`done` or
`superseded`) out of `docs/development/QUEUE.md` VERBATIM and appends it here, and refuses the
move unless every id occurs exactly as often in the live ledger plus its archive after the move
as before. Rows arrive in the order they were archived. Find any id, live or archived, with
`node tools/ledger.mjs find <ID>`; rulings in these rows stay indexed by `tools/decided.mjs`.
The August roll (`QUEUE-2026-08.md`) is a separate closed file and is never appended to.

### REC-130 · done — landed `11cf4aca`, merged by CONDUCT #4, 2026-09-18. **AN UNSIGNED CASE DOCUMENT IS NO LONGER READABLE BY STRANGERS, AND ENUMERATION LEARNS NOTHING: anonymous callers, unknown tokens, members of another project, the probe class and another member's agent all receive the BYTE-IDENTICAL answer a nonexistent case id gets — status, content type and body compared raw against the same op's answer for the same id read before it was minted. A signed case stays public.** Premise confirmed first: the unedited tree returned every authored sentence to an anonymous caller. Standing reuses the existing D-15 viewer predicate against the owning project — no narrower rule invented. **A SECOND disclosure found and closed at the same boundary:** `op=caseratify`'s refusal details told a member of another project that a case existed. `casesign.test.mjs`'s anonymous-read assertion corrected with a DATED comment; `gate-reads` moves `casedocument` to GATED. Controls (e)–(h) incl. the liar (`NOT_PERMITTED` instead of not-found → every byte-for-byte arm fails) and over-strictness. IC-141 MAJOR, I3 27.0.0. **Open on deployed instances until the next DIST cut.** **Prior state, kept as the record: running** — **SPAWNED 2026-09-18 by CONDUCT #4 into REC-126's slot — a correction to landed substrate, ahead of new work (BOB #14). DEPENDS-ON CHECKED AGAINST THE CODE at spawn: `casedocument` present in `bio-plane/src/index.mjs`'s OPS table with no credential class (the exposure this row closes). Falsify rather than believe: a live worker holds an `agent-*` worktree with a claim on the paths its scope names; if none does, this row is UNDETERMINED between `queued` and done-awaiting-integration — READ THE BRANCH, and never conclude `queued` from the absence alone.** — **AN UNSIGNED CASE DOCUMENT — a group's working material — IS READABLE BY ANYONE WITH NO LOGIN, AND CASE IDS ARE SEQUENTIAL, SO A STRANGER CAN WALK THEM.** `op=casedocument` carries no credential class and returns scope, findings, completeness statement, exclusions and bias acknowledgement to any caller. Found by REC-126's builder, checked at the code. **DECIDED by BOB #14, as an application of the publication fence already ruled (no new doctrine):** an UNSIGNED case document answers ONLY to members with standing in the owning project (and, once REC-126 exists, a live review-copy grant holder); **everyone else gets EXACTLY the answer a case that does not exist gets, so enumeration learns nothing;** a SIGNED case document stays public, because strangers need it to verify. CASE-5b's anonymous read was a mechanism choice with no ruling behind it. — owner RECORD.

A SIGNED case document stays public. **Correct `bio-plane/test/casesign.test.mjs`'s anonymous-read assertion with a DATED comment saying why the old one was wrong** — never exempt it. Grep every other reader of an unsigned case (and anything that enumerates case ids) and apply the same rule, or name why it does not apply.

Corpus: COFF-6's, re-listed from source and **IDENTICAL to CAP-7's M-13 read** (43,283 keys / 44 list requests); OOXML **762/762 a CENSUS**, PDF **1,000/27,783 a SAMPLE and literally M-13's own seeded draw** — the `random.sample` delegated to python3 with CAP-7's seed, so it is the same thousand documents. 1,762 documents, 6.60 GB, 0 fetch failures. **Per captured page** 1,302 B mean, p95 3,701, max 21,224, **with 26.3% of pages recovering NO text** (scans — indexed as nothing, never as empty). **Per document** 31,612 B mean, max 1,354,686. **Index bytes per text byte on workerd's SQLite: 1.998 at unit grain against 1.492 at document grain, so the unit grain costs 568 B/unit — the price of a hit being an ADDRESS.** The ratio **is not scale-free** (5.49 over a 75 B mean unit) and is quoted with its mean unit or not at all, which is the honest form of a figure that would otherwise be carried as a constant. **Promote CPU `ms = 0.0076 × units + 0.054 × KiB`, and the corpus's worst docx is 84.8% of the 40M window — §4.1's chunking remedy is REQUIRED, not optional.** Storage: 63,153 B per indexed PDF, +35.7% on D-190's per-bundle figure. `TEXT_CAP` 131,072 B KEPT on evidence (largest of 148,413 units is 21,224 B — 6.2× headroom), with the alternative and the reversal cost at the site; per capture, 2 MiB of extracted text, one number for every container. Seven control arms, all as declared: an empty corpus REFUSES, an all-failed-fetch REFUSES, a corpus of ONE measures n=1, a 0-byte page among real ones is a DATUM, an all-zero corpus refuses only the pages-with-text figure, and the copied `needsTier2` MATCHES `index.mjs`'s. Gates green, class FULL, against its own pristine baseline of 195/195 · 12,100 — **whose first reading was void and LOOKED HEALTHY at 194/195 · 12,024 · exit 0**, an independent reproduction of the three-package trap now in `CLAUDE.md`. **THE FINDING WORTH MORE THAN THE FOUR NUMBERS, rowed as M0-35 / D-368: the reference-iteration CPU currency is NOT runtime-portable** — `burn()` reports 25,032 iter/ms in node against 155,538 inside workerd, 6.21×, one machine one minute — and the node half corroborates CONTENT-PDF's own figure to within 4%, **so the disagreement is between RUNTIMES, not between dates**. The worker did NOT re-take or correct another area's row and said so, which is right: re-denominating another area's measurement from outside it is how a wrong number acquires a second author. **DESIGN GAP folded into `CONTENT-SEARCH-DESIGN.md` §4.1's Incomplete list: `slide-shape` CANNOT be written from I2** — `pptx.mjs` emits one text string per SLIDE, and `walkSlide()` keeps a shape index for hyperlinks then discards it at the line where it pushes a paragraph's text; `textchain.mjs` sharpens rather than settles it, since `readingSource()` requires both `slide` and `shape` while `covers()` accepts a shape-omitted extent. The worker measured the per-SLIDE unit and NAMED the substitution rather than quoting a figure for a unit that does not exist. Two instrument defects found and corrected AT THE CAUSE (the `undetermined` marker names itself `reason` in the PDF path and `why` in `ooxml.mjs`, so reading only `reason` scored 18 over-bound workbooks as an unnamed null — **the OOXML half was re-walked rather than the figure patched**). Every text figure is a FLOOR and the row says what it is blind to. One M id burned by piping `mintid` through `tail`, when the id line is at the HEAD — the repository's own read-it-unpiped lesson in a new costume.

landed: merged at `3877671`. **THE CENSUS RETURNED A PARTIAL ORDER, AND THAT IS THE RESULT RATHER THAN A SHORTFALL IN IT.** Scaled to the 29,626 text-bearing items of a 44,076-item population from a 600-document fixed-seed body sample: agenda 3,456 ±761 (a CONTROL — already registered), staff_report 3,012 ±716, minutes 2,617 ±673, ordinance_res 1,629 ±540, directory 395 ±272. **The comparison that settles the order is PAIRED, not a reading of overlapping intervals** — all five counts come from one sample — and it separates minutes from ordinances (z=2.27) and ordinances from directories (z=3.95) but **DOES NOT separate staff reports from minutes (z=0.78)**. §2's own rule is *minutes first unless the count says otherwise*; the count does not say otherwise, **so FW-18 writes minutes, staff reports, ordinances/resolutions, directories** — the default holding because the measurement declined to overturn it, which is a stronger reason than the default never being tested. **DIVERGENCE FROM THIS ROW'S OWN WORDING, reported rather than smoothed: the row declared the unclassified tally would RISE under a neutered class. It does not, and should not.** The row assumed two buckets where this census has three, and folding *read, no class* into *could not classify* would hide 247 readable documents behind the same label as 54 with no text layer — exactly what the row's own instruction to *print what you could NOT classify, NAMED* prevents. Conservation, the property the row was protecting, holds and is asserted: 111 + 247 + 52 + 190 = 600. **CONDUCT accepts the divergence: the worker followed the row's PURPOSE over its letter and said so, which is the behaviour the loop wants.** 58 control arms, 0 failed, each class neutered ALONE against the real sample. **Eight defects found by its own instruments, none smoothed:** five in the recogniser, all one class (a REFERENCE to a kind mistaken for MEMBERSHIP); three in the reader (24.5 MB of binary garbage from one report, caught by a function-word test; a regex that backtracked catastrophically and could not finish one PDF in five minutes; a kerned-run join turning `OAKLAND` into `O A K L A ND`); **and one control arm that asserted `rise + (held − rise) == held` — true for every value, asserting NOTHING — caught by reading its own output rather than its exit code.** Thresholds are NOT pre-registered and the file says so at the site: calibrated on twelve hand-checked documents, untouched after the 600 were drawn. **What it cannot see, measured rather than asserted:** an image stratum bounded at ~905 keys (~2%) by a header probe; name-layer recall MEASURED at 13% for staff reports and 0% for directories, so **a filename census would have ranked staff reports FOURTH**; and 31.7% of sampled documents unreadable by its crude tier-1 instrument with no ToUnicode CMap support — a fact about that instrument, NOT evidence about the plane's reader and NOT an OCR requirement. **For FW-18: 52 of 600 documents satisfied MORE THAN ONE class, so a content type assuming one document is one kind will mis-describe about 1 in 12; §2 now says so.** Its report also raised the `decided.mjs` marker defect, confirmed and filed as D-367 / M0-34. Two M ids burned reading mintid's output before matching its first line; gaps cost nothing by the tool's own header.

### M0-40 · done — landed `f9b0f085`, merged at `2fa9c85d` by CONDUCT #1, 2026-09-16. **THE ROW OFFERED TWO ROUTES AND THE ANSWER IS THE SECOND: the classifier CANNOT be taught to follow a local binding, because doing so OVER-COLLECTS** — and the reason the hoist defeats it is the finding: **the INLINE spelling was being credited with amplification it never had.** A loop's extent begins at its `for` KEYWORD, so a scan in the loop's own HEADER is scored as a scan PER ROW when it is the loop's row source and runs exactly once — **and 21 of the 35 memberships rest on that credit alone.** All three corrections were DRIVEN off the classifier's own text: `for…of` only → 46; every loop form → 56, **which enrols `ncLinear` itself, the fixture the suite already declares BY NAME as NOT this class**; remove the header credit → 14. Measured twice by readers sharing no code path, agreeing on the same names. **SO THE ITEM CHANGED NOTHING AND THAT IS CORRECT** — classifier byte-identical, both measured constants untouched, no method enters or leaves. What landed is REC-88's hoist as a TRANSFORM DRIVEN ON EVERY MEMBER: HOIST-FRAGILE (21), HOIST-STABLE (4), and **the 10 the transform cannot reach NAMED AS UNREACHED rather than scored stable** — scoring an unreachable thing clean is how a ratchet quietly stops measuring. **D-384 raised for the decision that is not a worker's.** **TWO ARMS CAME BACK WITH MORE THAN DECLARED AND THE CAUSE IS STRUCTURAL:** a method cannot join this class without also gaining an unbounded row source, so a class-count-neutral swap NECESSARILY moves the census by one — **the two ratchets in that file cannot move independently.** **AND A NEAR-MISS THAT NEARLY DESTROYED ANOTHER SESSION'S WORK:** force-push being denied, it converted a rebase into a merge, and restoring its saved resolved files **silently discarded BOB's 33 new lines in `MEASUREMENTS.md` — the hash matched its OWN copy perfectly, which is exactly why it looked right.** Caught by diffing against `origin/main` and finding it suspiciously empty. That is the `git checkout --` trap in a new coat: **a restore is believable only when measured against what you were supposed to PRESERVE, not against what you SAVED.** It checked CONDUCT #1's UNREAD_FORMS widening deliberately and kept every word. **M0-44 is now unblocked.** **Prior state, kept as the record: running, then queued.** Falsify rather than believe: a live worker holds an `agent-*` worktree with a claim on the paths its scope names; **if none does, this row is UNDETERMINED between `queued` and done-awaiting-integration — READ THE BRANCH (the preamble's falsification rule), and never conclude `queued` from the absence alone.** **Prior state, kept as the record: queued** — **NOT SPAWNED IN THE 2026-09-15 SECOND WAVE, and the reason is on the row rather than left to be investigated: it edits `bio-plane/test/derivation-bounds.test.mjs`, which M0-38 holds for that wave.** Two workers in one file is the collision this session spent a day merging out of other people's branches. Next wave, and nothing else about it has changed. — **THE BOUNDS CLASSIFIER READS AMPLIFICATION OFF A LOOP WHOSE ITERABLE IS A ROW SOURCE, SO ASSIGNING THAT SCAN TO A LOCAL FIRST SCORES ZERO AND READS CLEAN — same query, same rows, same work, and the method LEAVES the roster.** Found by REC-88's first draft doing exactly that, caught only because the roster FLOOR noticed the departure. — waits on nothing; the M0 background lane holds no slot.

scope: **START BY STATING WHAT CANNOT BE DONE, because this row's worst outcome is a mechanism that LOOKS like proof of execution and is not.** Proving that a control ran is not achievable from inside the repository: any artifact a worker can write, a worker can write without running anything. **The most that is honestly available is a DATED RUN TOKEN whose content nobody can produce without the run** — a figure the arm itself prints, a digest of its own output, an exit status captured to a file — and the row must say plainly that this raises the cost of a false claim rather than making one impossible. **A register that claims to prove execution would be a worse instrument than the one that admits it cannot**, which is the whole subject of M0-41 one level in. Design the token, state its limit at the site, and make a DECLARED-but-not-RUN arm distinguishable from a RUN one in the register's own output.

And the arm that proves the token is not decoration: a token forged without the run must be detectable, or the row must state at the site that it is not.

Routed onto M0-39 with the position, the method and the class. **ITS BASELINE IS THE FIRST OF NINE TO CONFIRM THE BRIEFED FIGURE RATHER THAN CORRECT IT, and HOW it established that is the point:** a pristine scratch tree read 204/205 · 12,685 · exit 1 with `acquire.test.mjs` red; rather than accept or dismiss it the worker ran the suite ALONE (84 pass, exit 0), read the failure as `SQLITE_IOERR_SHMOPEN` inside workerd, and confirmed **8 concurrent batteries** — then showed 204+1 = 205 and 12,685+84 = 12,769, the brief's figures exactly. **A red established as the MACHINE rather than the tree, by arithmetic rather than by a second run.** **Six defects in its own instruments, all recorded rather than smoothed** — four false gaps (including a WRAPPED IMPORT a line-based reader could not cross, in a blind spot it had not declared, and a `fail`/`FAIL` case mismatch that made an arm assert over an EMPTY LIST: an equality costing nothing, inside the harness built to refuse those); `waitquiet --check` READ THROUGH A PIPE reporting `exit 0` beside the word BUSY (`CLAUDE.md`'s own pipe trap); and **the row's own rule catching the row** — the `hygiene` cell was first written from that instrument's COMMENT (21/3/18) and prints 34/24/10 when RUN. **A RUN-DISCIPLINE FINDING WORTH MORE THAN ITS ITEM: a battery reached 165/205 with ZERO failures, was SIGTERMed, and the harness notification read "exit code 0" — the wrapper's status — while the battery's own echo read `BATTERY EXIT=143`. A truncated run containing no failures is INDISTINGUISHABLE from a green one if you read the notification instead of the status.** **ONE CLAIM IN ITS REPORT IS FALSE AND IS CORRECTED HERE RATHER THAN ROUTED: act 7 says `kickoffs/FRAMEWORK.md` "still does not name the plane bundle". It does** — the section `docprofile/ IS AN INPUT TO THE PLANE'S COMMITTED BUNDLE` landed at FW-18's integration and is present at lines 86-92 on the tree the census measured. **A world-claim, settled by the artifact, and the artifact says otherwise.** Everything else in the report checked out. **Zero files touched under `bio-plane/src`, `checks`, `scripts`, `tools/`, `civicos-ui/` or `newgroup/`**; its driver is deliberately not a `.test.mjs` (the `m025-arm-census.mjs` precedent) so no floor moves — verified, corpus stayed 197 plane + 8 fleet. The diffstat would not have shown it (insertions and deletions in one file is what a legitimate refinement looks like). Caught by checking the merged file HEADING BY HEADING against main, then a line-level check for anything else; restored verbatim in its own commit (`20ddfc7`) before the merge.** **Prior state, kept as the record: queued** — **WHICH OF THIS PROJECT'S INSTRUMENTS ARE REQUIRED, AND WHICH MERELY EXIST? ### M0-54 · done — landed `f88707dd` + `64f4b62e`, merged at `de288de` by CONDUCT #2, 2026-09-17. **THE HEADLINE OVERTURNS PART OF D-288's RULING AND IS RECORDED AS SUCH RATHER THAN SOFTENED: 6 LANDED / 3 UNINTEGRATED / 0 UNDETERMINED — the dominant cause is LANDED at 6 of 9 (67%), so *a remote `worktree-agent-*` branch MEANS UNINTEGRATED WORK* is WRONG FOR TWO BRANCHES IN EVERY THREE over the historical set.** That is exactly the outcome this row named as most valuable and least expected, and it arrived as a COUNT rather than an impression. **Four landed-but-rebased-away** (M0-38, REC-60, REC-95, IS-6) — own commit subject present in `origin/main` history under a DIFFERENT sha, 92.3–98.5% line survival — **two landed by effect** (CPDF-10's deliverable on main at `ef3dfd3d`; REC-84's duplicate D-349 row 2 → 1), **three genuinely unintegrated** (D-254, UI-43, D-270) at 1.2–7.8% with four suites absent from main. **THE RESULT IS BIMODAL WITH NOTHING BETWEEN — 7.8% to 92.3% IS THE WHOLE GAP — which is WHY `0 UNDETERMINED` is a finding rather than a convenience: the data separated itself and the worker said so instead of presenting a clean number as though judgement had produced it.** **THE DISCRIMINATION CONTROL IS STRONGER THAN THE ROW ASKED FOR, and arm B is the one nobody would have thought to run.** Arm A drove the liar's check this row NAMED — *does `CLAIMS.md` exist on main* — and it passes **9/9 with no power**, as predicted. **Arm B then showed `CLAIMS.md` survival is UNCORRELATED rather than merely weak: `IS-6` is PROVABLY LANDED and scores 0% on it**, so keying on the shared append-only file does not just lack power, **it ACTIVELY MISCLASSIFIES A LANDED BRANCH** — the difference between *this check is weak* and *this check is wrong*. Arm C re-ran the real instrument across subjects: IS-6 scores 92.3% on its own lines and **1.6%** on UI-43's. **THE CORROBORATION IS GENUINE AND ITS INDEPENDENCE WAS ESTABLISHED RATHER THAN ASSERTED:** the three unintegrated are EXACTLY D-288's own 2026-08-10 backup push, reached by a content check that never referenced that list — **two witnesses, not one source copied**, which is this estate's standing warning honoured in the one place it would have been easiest to skip. **D-270's subject defect re-verified at the artifact and STILL LIVE** (`sessionOpGate`, `CONTROL_PLANE_REFUSAL_CHECKS` and the whole C-39 family absent from main), with the legacy sentence's 5 sites recorded as **a POINTER AND NOT A PROOF — sites counted, ops not driven, stated UNDETERMINED.** **Dispositions: 6 PRUNED and verified 9 → 3 from `ls-remote` rather than from a cached ref; the three unintegrated ROWED as `D-397` and NEVER MERGED, which was its own acceptance text; census and controls in `M-42`.** It rowed in `DEBT.md` rather than `QUEUE.md` because the queue is CONDUCT's sole ground — correct, and it said why. **GATE PROFILE RULED BY CONDUCT #2 AS `DOCS`, ON A MEASUREMENT AND NOT AS A CONCESSION TO THE DISK:** `gates.mjs` classifies the diff DOCS and CONDUCT verified it at the artifact — four paths, every one under `docs/`, no code — so the doc-facing suites plus `plancheck` were the owed gate and a full battery was never owed — **and in the event the worker delivered one anyway, green, which makes the profile question moot rather than resolved in anybody's favour.** **THE WORKER ESCALATED RATHER THAN GUESSING WHEN IT BELIEVED THE MACHINE COULD NOT DELIVER A BATTERY — AND THEN RETRACTED ITS OWN MEASUREMENT BEFORE CONDUCT COULD PUBLISH IT, WHICH IS THE BEST THING IN THIS ROW.** It reported *40 seconds of CPU in 68 minutes* as evidence of a starved run, CONDUCT credited that as a measurement of the machine — **and the worker came back to say it was reading the CPU time of the PARENT `battery.mjs`, which IDLES while its per-suite children do the work. It had measured the supervisor's idleness and inferred a starved fleet.** The run in fact completed in **406.4s at 213/213 suites green · 13,345 assertions · 0 skipped**, provenance confirming it ran against its own commit `64f4b62e`. **CONDUCT'S LANDED LINE WAS CORRECTED BEFORE THE PUSH RATHER THAN AFTER, so the wrong number never entered `origin/main`** — and the worker's own words are the reason it is recorded at all: *I'd rather hand back the praise than let a wrong number enter the record under my name — that is the same failure my own item exists to catch, committed by me while auditing it.* **THE GENERAL FORM IS WORTH MORE THAN THE INCIDENT: measuring a SUPERVISOR and concluding about its WORKERS is the wrong-process class, and it produces a confident number in the direction of alarm** — the same shape as reading a wrapper's exit status instead of the battery's own. **What IS real and is carried forward is the raw figure: 1.6 GiB free at 100%, unchanged across every gate.** The escalation itself was still correct conduct: refusing to report a green or a red it could not separate from the machine is exactly the instruction, and a red recorded as a defect when the cause was the volume is a false finding that outlives the disk problem by months. **WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT DO TO D-288, stated so the next reader does not over-read it:** D-288's realised cost was REC-91 reaching nobody, and ITEM 1 — the worker pushing its own branch — fixes that at the only actor guaranteed alive. **That half is untouched and proven.** What this row narrows is the SIGNAL: the branch list is an audit trail for a failure item 1 now prevents, and pruning keeps that trail legible. **The honest conclusion is not that the ruling was wrong but that the estate has a SECOND residue nobody rowed — the LOCAL WORKTREE, which the harness locks and nothing can reclaim — and that one is the harness's rather than ours.** **Prior state, kept as the record: running** — **SPAWNED 2026-09-17 by CONDUCT #2** — worktree-isolated, `claude-opus-5` pinned at spawn, slot 4 of a FOUR-worker wave, the second of this session, **flipped in the SAME TURN as the previous wave's last integration rather than after a report — CONDUCT #1 measured that the dangerous moment is not a worker failing but the last integration SUCCEEDING, and sat idle 9h20m with a green board.** **SIZED DOWN FROM FIVE TO FOUR ON A MEASUREMENT TAKEN THIS TURN: the harness LOCKS an agent worktree when its agent finishes, and three of the last wave's five could not be removed even though their work was merged and `plancheck` certified `0 EXPOSED`. So a wave permanently strands roughly 635 MB per locked worker.** Free disk is 5.2 GiB at 98%, recovered from a trough of 2.9 GiB at 99%. **THE SIGNAL IS NOW CLEAN AND THE ROW IS EXACTLY ITS CONTENTS.** CONDUCT #2 pruned 16 branches this session, every one verified an ancestor of `origin/main`, taking the remote list from 22 to **NINE — and those nine are precisely this row's set.** So the measurement is no longer cluttered by integrated work and the only question left is the one the row asks. **Re-take the list yourself rather than trusting the row's snapshot; it was accurate when written and the population moves.** **Falsify rather than believe:** a live worker holds an `agent-*` worktree with a claim on the paths this row's scope names; **if none does, this row is UNDETERMINED between `queued` and done-awaiting-integration — READ THE BRANCH (the preamble's falsification rule), and never conclude `queued` from the absence alone.** **THE REMOTE BRANCH LIST IS A SIGNAL NOW, AND ITS FIRST READING SAYS NINE BRANCHES NEED ASSESSMENT — BUT "NOT AN ANCESTOR OF `origin/main`" HAS TWO CAUSES AND THIS ROW EXISTS SO NOBODY RESOLVES IT BY THE CONVENIENT ONE.** — waits on nothing; the M0 background lane holds no slot.

scope: **THE MEASUREMENT, taken 2026-09-17 by CONDUCT #2 at M0-49's own integration, which is the first moment it could be taken.** D-288's ruling is that **with pruning, a `worktree-agent-*` branch on the remote MEANS UNINTEGRATED WORK** — the list becomes a WORKLIST rather than noise. The list had never been pruned, so its first reading was noise by construction. **CONDUCT #2 pruned every branch it could PROVE integrated — 13 in total, all verified `git merge-base --is-ancestor <tip> origin/main`, which means the content is on the remote by definition and nothing can be lost — taking the list from 22 to 11.** Two of the surviving 11 belong to live workers of this wave. **NINE REMAIN AND THEY ARE THE ROW.**

**WHAT MUST NOT BE CONCLUDED, and it is written here because the conclusion is one command away and would be wrong:** these nine are **NOT** established as unintegrated work. `kickoffs/CONDUCT.md`'s own prune section names the false positive exactly — **a branch merged and then rebased away by a later `git rebase origin/main` on `main` stops being an ancestor even though its content landed.** So each of the nine is **UNDETERMINED between (a) genuinely unintegrated work sitting on the remote and (b) work that landed and whose merge was rebased away.** That is the unearned-absence class in D-288's own instrument, and reading the nine as a backlog of lost work would be this project's most-repeated defect committed inside the mechanism built to refuse it.

**SO THE METHOD IS FIXED AND IT IS NOT ANCESTRY: CHECK FOR THE CONTENT.** `--is-ancestor` proves a merge HAPPENED and does not prove the content SURVIVED, and it answers TRUE for a merge that was later reverted — both edges are recorded in `kickoffs/CONDUCT.md`. For each of the nine, read what the branch ADDED — a file, an op, a symbol, a suite — and ask whether it is in `origin/main` TODAY (`git cat-file -e origin/main:<path>`, `git show origin/main:<file> | grep -c '<symbol>'`). **The queue row is bookkeeping and lags; the tree is the fact.**

**THE NINE, captured with their tips so the next reader starts from a measurement rather than re-deriving the set** (they will have moved — re-take it): `a29f17e083aa0b5ef` @ `0e2c0cad` · `a5b2e8e66fda4f115` @ `ab268fce` · `a61e489de171ae6c5` @ `9e24ef6e` · `a90a87bcb7f131e59` @ `1f5f95fa` · `a9e7e017d06799858` @ `9706d19e` · `aa10d195065b703e8` @ `b676b4f8` · `aafee89563a3f2d42` @ `484ed359` · `adefd8db6571e8b30` @ `3fb28b81` · `ae95c3be71f5bd167` @ `82401bc1`.

**AND THE OUTCOME THAT WOULD BE MOST VALUABLE IS THE ONE NOBODY EXPECTS: FINDING THAT ALL NINE LANDED.** That would establish the rebased-away cause as the DOMINANT one, which makes the remote list a WEAKER signal than D-288's ruling assumes and is a finding about the mechanism rather than about the branches. **Say which it is with a count, not an impression.**
accepts-when: each of the nine is classified **LANDED** (with the path or symbol found in `origin/main` that proves it) or **UNINTEGRATED** (with what it holds that `origin/main` lacks) — **and a branch that cannot be classified either way is reported as UNDETERMINED with the reason, never defaulted**; anything found genuinely unintegrated is ROWED with what it holds and what integrating it costs, never merged by this item; anything found landed is PRUNED with `git push origin --delete`, and the prune verified from `git ls-remote` rather than from a local ref; **the dominant cause is STATED with its count**, because the ratio is the finding about D-288's signal. `node tools/plancheck.mjs` 0 fail, and its `stranded work:` note re-read after the sweep.
NEGATIVE CONTROL: run and recorded — **before pruning anything, take one branch you have classified LANDED and confirm the content check FAILS for a symbol it never added**, so the check is shown to discriminate rather than to pass over everything; and confirm a branch classified UNINTEGRATED **names something `origin/main` genuinely lacks**, checked at the artifact. **State how a liar satisfies this before stating what it checks:** the cheapest green is to classify all nine LANDED by finding *some* file each one touched that exists on main — every branch touches `CLAIMS.md`, so a check keyed on a shared append-only file passes over everything and establishes nothing. **The check must key on what the branch UNIQUELY added.**

### M0-52 · done — landed `1d4a3736`, merged at `e083416` by CONDUCT #2, 2026-09-17. **BOTH DOORS CLOSED AT THE RIGHT ALTITUDE — *an allocation must be UNAMBIGUOUS TO ITS CALLER* — rather than as two patches.** Door one: a known-flag whitelist refuses before any allocating line, **names the offending token AND names `--floor-only`**, because the failure mode is precisely someone who wanted to LOOK and mistyped the name of looking. Door two: the minted id is restated by **TWO INDEPENDENT MECHANISMS — on STDERR (survives any stdout filter) and on the LAST STDOUT LINE (survives `2>/dev/null`) — each covering the filter the other loses.** **THE WHITELIST IS DERIVED FROM THE TOOL'S OWN SOURCE, not hand-carried**, with a suite arm that re-greps every `flag(...)`/`val(...)` and fails by name IN BOTH DIRECTIONS — because every hand-kept list in this estate has gone stale, which is M0-43's measured defect one tool over. **THE SHAPE WAS DECIDED BY THE RECURRENCE RATHER THAN BY PREFERENCE: `D-289` prescribed *run it bare and read all of it* — correct, written down, and the third occurrence happened anyway — so the fix had to be a MECHANISM and not a better warning**, which is `kickoffs/CONDUCT.md`'s own finding about vigilance arriving against the one tool built to retire it. **THE CRITERION WAS THE LEDGER AND NOT THE MESSAGE, which is the half that matters: door one pre-change `M0 --show` MINTED `M0-55` at exit 0 with the ledger going 0 → 3 files; post-change exit 2 with the ledger 0 → 0.** Door two pre-change, `M0 | tail -1` showed a scope line and NO ID while an id had been allocated; post-change all four filter shapes surface it. Six door-one suite arms count claim files before and after, and under control they fail as `[0,1,false]` — **naming the ALLOCATION, not a status.** **OVER-STRICTNESS SWEPT ACROSS 17 DOCUMENTED INVOCATIONS: zero lines lost, zero exits moved, zero ids moved** — `--list`, `--list <NS>`, `--floor-only`, `--audit`, `--audit --base` and `--json` byte-identical on BOTH streams. **Stated exactly rather than overclaimed: the MINTING forms gain one appended line each, which IS the fix, with every pre-existing line unchanged and the same ids allocated — verified against ledger claim files rather than against output text.** **ZERO IDS BURNED, AND FOR THIS ROW THAT IS THE DATA POINT: both doors were driven in a SANDBOX LEDGER via `BIO_IDALLOC_DIR`, so proving the defect cost the real ledger nothing.** CONDUCT re-drove both doors on the MERGED tree and confirms it: `M0 --show` refuses with *NOTHING WAS MINTED and the ledger did not move*; a filtered read shows `MINTED …` on the last line; and the real ledger's floor is UNMOVED at M0-54. **TWO FINDINGS RECORDED RATHER THAN SMOOTHED, both instrument defects the worker fixed in the INSTRUMENT and not the subject:** its first over-strictness check matched the literal string `M0-52` inside the new lines' own citation of this row and reported `IDS MOVED` on six arms where nothing moved; and **control arm (16) FAILED WIDER THAN DECLARED — dropping `--who` also disarmed the whole eight-process race section, because that driver passes `--who`** — the over-strictness hazard at full size, inside the controls themselves. Battery **213/213 · 13,374 · 0 skipped**, baseline 213/213 · 13,344 matching CONDUCT #2's exactly, **the +30 attributed per suite (`mintid.test.mjs` 83 → 113) with a diff of all 213 showing NO OTHER SUITE MOVED**; `--strict` exit 0 unpiped; `plancheck --local` 0 fail post-commit. **`D-395`'s gap row already pointed here and needs no edit; `D-289`'s third-occurrence finding is what this row answers.** **Prior state, kept as the record: running** — **SPAWNED 2026-09-17 by CONDUCT #2** — worktree-isolated, `claude-opus-5` pinned at spawn, slot 3 of a FOUR-worker wave, the second of this session, **flipped in the SAME TURN as the previous wave's last integration rather than after a report — CONDUCT #1 measured that the dangerous moment is not a worker failing but the last integration SUCCEEDING, and sat idle 9h20m with a green board.** **SIZED DOWN FROM FIVE TO FOUR ON A MEASUREMENT TAKEN THIS TURN: the harness LOCKS an agent worktree when its agent finishes, and three of the last wave's five could not be removed even though their work was merged and `plancheck` certified `0 EXPOSED`. So a wave permanently strands roughly 635 MB per locked worker.** Free disk is 5.2 GiB at 98%, recovered from a trough of 2.9 GiB at 99%. **Both doors are on the row and the second arrived after it was written, so read the whole scope.** Door one: an unrecognised flag behind a VALID NAMESPACE is discarded and the allocating default runs. Door two, found the same day by a different worker: piping the output through a filter hides the `MINTED` line, so the caller re-runs an ALLOCATING command to see what it got. **A fix closing only door one leaves the one that actually fires under this estate's working conditions.** Four ids are known burned (`IC-111`, `IC-113`, `M0-53`, `D-395`) and the gap is recorded as `D-395`; the cost is honestly small and the row says so — do not inflate it. **Falsify rather than believe:** a live worker holds an `agent-*` worktree with a claim on the paths this row's scope names; **if none does, this row is UNDETERMINED between `queued` and done-awaiting-integration — READ THE BRANCH (the preamble's falsification rule), and never conclude `queued` from the absence alone.** **`tools/mintid.mjs <NS> --<anything>` SILENTLY PERFORMS THE ALLOCATING DEFAULT. scope: **MEASURED AT THE ARTIFACT BY CONDUCT #2 ON 2026-09-17, NOT CARRIED FROM THE REPORT THAT RAISED IT — and the measurement NARROWED the claim, which is why it was taken.** REC-96's worker reported that *an unrecognised flag performs the allocating default silently*, having burned `IC-111` and `IC-113` calling `mintid.mjs IC --show`. **Driven here, that is true in one form and FALSE in another, and the difference is the whole defect.** `node tools/mintid.mjs --definitely-not-a-flag` prints USAGE and mints nothing — the safe behaviour, already built. `node tools/mintid.mjs M0 --show` **MINTED `M0-53`**, printing `1 id(s) ALREADY HELD and stepped over: 52`. **So the guard exists and is bypassed by the presence of a valid namespace: the unrecognised flag is not rejected, it is DISCARDED, and the tool falls through to its irreversible default.**

**WHAT MAKES THIS WORSE THAN A PAPERCUT, and it is the argument for the row rather than a spot fix.** (1) **A READ-ONLY FORM EXISTS** — `--floor-only` reports the floor and allocates nothing — **so the failure mode is specifically a user who wanted to LOOK and mistyped the name of looking.** (2) **The tool's entire argument is that you should call it WITHOUT THINKING.** `kickoffs/CONDUCT.md` says in so many words that the vigilance fix was already tried and failed, that every brief for two days told workers to measure first and every one of them did, and that the remedy was to *write the command, not a better warning*. **A command that punishes a typo with a silent irreversible write reintroduces the vigilance it was built to retire, in the one place this project decided vigilance does not work.** (3) It is the silent-wrong-act class: **a step that PUBLISHES and a step that MAKES IT TRUE are two steps** — here they are fused, and the user's intent was neither.

**THE COST IS SMALL AND MUST BE STATED HONESTLY RATHER THAN INFLATED, because overstating it is this project's primary threat model pointed at its own backlog.** A burned id is a GAP, the ledger says gaps are expected and cost nothing, and the real price is one grep at a renumber sweep — **one of which already missed a REGEX LITERAL, where `C-29\.` is not the text `C-29.`.** Three ids are known burned to this defect today (`IC-111`, `IC-113`, and `M0-53`, which is MINE, burned deliberately to verify the claim rather than carry it onto this row unverified — that is the price of the measurement and it is recorded rather than hidden). **So this is not urgent and it is not nothing: it is a sharp edge on the one tool every worker is instructed to call blind.**

**A SECOND DOOR ONTO THIS DEFECT ARRIVED WITHIN THE HOUR, FROM A DIFFERENT WORKER, AND IT IS THE MORE DANGEROUS ONE — FOLDED IN HERE BECAUSE A ROW NAMING ONE DOOR INVITES A FIX THAT CLOSES ONE DOOR.** M0-51's worker burned **`D-395`** the same afternoon, and not through a flag at all: **it piped `mintid`'s output through `tail`, which CUT OFF THE LINE CARRYING THE MINTED ID, so it could not see what it had been given and RE-RAN AN ALLOCATING COMMAND TO FIND OUT.** Verified at the artifact: the tool prints `MINTED <NS>-<n>` as its FIRST line and the ledger/floor detail on the lines after it, so **`mintid <NS> | tail -1` shows the ledger line and never the id.** That is this project's own pipe trap — *a pipeline reports the LAST stage's status, so every filter you add to make the output readable also throws away the answer you were filtering for* — **fused to an irreversible write, and the causation runs the wrong way: the output being unreadable is what CAUSES the second allocation.**

**SO THE TWO DOORS ARE ONE DEFECT AT A HIGHER ALTITUDE AND THE FIX MUST BE STATED AT THAT ALTITUDE: AN ALLOCATION MUST BE UNAMBIGUOUS TO ITS CALLER, AND TODAY IT IS AMBIGUOUS IN BOTH DIRECTIONS.** Door one: the caller asked to LOOK and the tool WROTE (an unrecognised flag discarded behind a valid namespace). Door two: the caller WROTE and could not tell WHAT, so wrote again (the id on a line a filter removed). **A fix that only rejects unknown flags leaves door two wide open, and it is the one that fires under exactly the conditions this estate runs in** — a worker reading a long tool's output through a filter, which every brief effectively encourages. **Candidates worth weighing rather than a prescription:** put the minted id on the LAST line as well as the first, or on stderr where a stdout filter cannot eat it; make `--json` the documented form for any programmatic read; and print the id again in any subsequent run's `ALREADY HELD and stepped over` note, which the tool already computes and which is the only reason `M0-53` was recoverable at all.

**AND THE ROW MUST NOT OVERSTATE THIS EITHER.** Four ids are now known burned to the pair — `IC-111`, `IC-113`, `M0-53` (CONDUCT's own, from verifying door one) and `D-395` — **out of a corpus the tool grades at 745 sites across 20 namespaces.** Gaps cost nothing by the ledger's own statement; the price is one grep at a renumber sweep. **This is a sharp edge on the tool every worker is told to call blind, not a leak.**

**DO NOT ASSUME THE FIX IS "REJECT UNKNOWN FLAGS" WITHOUT CHECKING WHAT ELSE RELIES ON THE PERMISSIVE PARSE.** Grep every call site — briefs, kickoffs, scripts, suites — before tightening, because a tool that starts refusing where it answered is a break, and a worker mid-item hitting a newly strict parser is a worse failure than a burned id.
accepts-when: `node tools/mintid.mjs <NS> --<unrecognised>` **REFUSES and allocates nothing**, with the message naming the unrecognised token AND pointing at `--floor-only` as the read-only form — driven, with the ledger read before and after to prove no id moved; every EXISTING flag combination still works, driven; **and the criterion may NOT be satisfied by a test that only asserts the refusal message** — the load-bearing assertion is that the LEDGER IS UNCHANGED, because a tool that prints a refusal and mints anyway is exactly the defect one layer deeper. `node tools/plancheck.mjs --local`, then BARE after committing; `cd bio-plane && npm run test:battery` green own-baseline.
NEGATIVE CONTROL: run and recorded — the refusal removed → `<NS> --show` mints again and the arm FAILS naming the allocated id and the ledger delta, **not merely the exit status**; over-strictness: every documented invocation (`<NS>`, `--list`, `--list <NS>`, `<NS> --floor-only`, `--count`, `--who`, `--why`, `--json`, `--audit --base`) behaves BYTE-IDENTICALLY after the change, because this row tightens what is REFUSED and must change nothing that WORKS. **State how a liar would satisfy this before stating what it checks:** the cheapest green is a parser that refuses everything unfamiliar including flags it should accept, which makes the arm pass and the tool unusable — so the over-strictness half is not a courtesy, it is the half that decides the row.

scope: **TWO ARMS, ONE SHAPE, and the shape is the finding: a convention nobody can check is a convention that holds until a busy day.** (1) **DUPLICATE IDS IN UNGRADED NAMESPACES.** **THE PREMISE THIS ROW WAS FIRST WRITTEN WITH WAS FALSE, and it is corrected here rather than quietly replaced because getting it wrong changed the proposed fix.** It said `mintid` does not grade `M`. **`mintid` DOES allocate `M`** — it is one of its seventeen namespaces (`M  prose  measurement entries`) and `node tools/mintid.mjs M --floor-only` answers. **What `M` lacks is a declared ALLOCATION SITE**, which is why `mintid --audit` reports `NOT COVERED  M — no allocation site is declared for this namespace, so a repeat cannot be told from a mention`. **So the four collisions were a BYPASS, not a gap in the allocator**: each worker read the corpus floor out of `MEASUREMENTS.md` and computed the next number — correct on every branch, wrong in the union — and the bypass left no site for the audit to see. (CONDUCT #11 renumbered them the same way and bypassed it too.) **So the fix is NOT to build an allocator that already exists.** It is to give `M` a recognisable allocation site so a BYPASS is visible to `--audit`, and to require the allocator at the point of minting — **an allocator nobody is required to call is a checker with extra steps.** Measured 2026-09-15: **four items filed `M-21`** — M0-34 (kept), COFF-11 (→ M-22), FW-18 (→ M-24) and REC-90 (→ M-23) — and **FW-18's reached `origin/main` at `a59ac7b` beside M0-34's and nothing failed.** The arm is a grep: no heading id in `MEASUREMENTS.md` (and the same for `C` wherever it is allocated) appears twice. **The direction is settled and the row says so rather than leaving it open: an allocator that REFUSES beats a checker that REPORTS, and `mintid` exists precisely because check-then-act has no atomicity — so the work is the SITE and the requirement to call it, not a second checker.** A duplicate-heading grep may still be worth having as a backstop; if you build it, say at the site that it is a backstop for a bypass and not the primary defence, or the next reader will take it for one. (2) **ATTRIBUTION.** `RULED by Bob` means DOCTRINE no session may revisit; a session's own name means MECHANISM a later session MAY revisit on evidence. Five landed plane comments call BOB #11's own correction (`9954a9c`) "Bob's ruling", raised by BOB #11 itself and corrected at this wave's close. **A mechanism decision wearing doctrine's attribution becomes UNREVISABLE IN PRACTICE** — the next reader works around the rule instead of correcting it — which is the more expensive direction. **THE CHECK IS WHETHER THE CITATION RESOLVES TO THE NAMED ACTOR, NOT WHETHER THE SENTENCE CONTAINS A WORD** (BOB #11's refinement, 2026-09-15, and it is sharper than the grep this row was first written with). **The tell is already in the corpus's own grammar: a ruling attributed to Bob names a DATE and a place he ruled it; a mechanism attributed to a session names the SESSION and its COMMIT.** So the arm resolves the citation beside the attribution and fails where the two disagree — an architect attribution citing a session-authored sha, or a session attribution citing a ruling of Bob's. **A banned-phrase list is the wrong instrument and would be worse than none**, because "RULED by Bob" is correct wherever he actually ruled and this corpus is full of places he did.
accepts-when: a planted duplicate `M-` heading FAILS `plancheck` by name, driven; a planted architect-attribution beside a session sha FAILS by name, driven, **and a planted SESSION attribution beside one of Bob's real rulings fails too — the arm must catch the mis-pairing in BOTH directions or it is only enforcing a house style**; **THE CHEAP DEFEAT IS NAMED HERE BECAUSE IT IS THE ONE THIS ARM INVITES (BOB #11): an arm satisfied by a corpus-wide rewrite of one phrase has VERIFIED NOTHING, because it can be satisfied by making every attribution uniformly wrong** — so the acceptance is that the arm resolves citations, demonstrated by it PASSING over a corpus containing both attribution forms correctly used and FAILING over one where the two forms have been swapped; **both arms run GREEN over the repository as it stands after this wave's corrections** — and if either finds something the wave missed, that is the row's first real output and it is fixed rather than exempted; `node tools/plancheck.mjs --local` 0 fail; `cd bio-plane && npm run test:battery` green own-baseline; `node scripts/coverage.mjs --strict` DIRECTLY, `$?` unpiped, exit 0.
NEGATIVE CONTROL: run and recorded — **the over-strictness arm is the one that decides whether this row is worth having**: a comment that correctly attributes a real Bob ruling (`RULED by Bob, 2026-07-30` in the framework is the model) must still PASS, and a legitimately re-used id form that is not a collision must still pass; the duplicate arm neutered → the four collisions this row was born from must reappear when re-planted, proving the check reads the file rather than a list of known cases.
correction: 2026-09-15 · CONDUCT #11 — **ARRIVING AFTER THE SPAWN AND THEREFORE MINE TO PAY AT INTEGRATION, not the worker's to have known.** M0-41's census (M-25) and BOB #11's independent re-drive both landed while this item was running. **THREE things change.** **(1) A THIRD SUBJECT, and it is the one that matters most: `plancheck`'s DEGRADE-TO-WARN arms.** With `corpuscheck.mjs` made unloadable, `plancheck` reads `0 fail, 2 warn` and **EXITS 0**, leaving the design corpus and the row-design rule UNVERIFIED. **CONDUCT's position, decided and not left open: an unloadable predicate must FAIL, not WARN** — `0 fail` is a statement about the corpus that the run did not make, and a reader taking exit 0 as *verified* has concluded a value from an absence with two causes (verified-clean, or not-looked-at), which is this queue's own corrected clause living inside the gate. **The brittleness counter-argument is answered rather than outweighed: emit a NAMED refusal (`PREDICATE_UNLOADABLE`, naming the file), so the message says WHICH check did not run instead of implying all of them did.** **FIX THE CLASS, NOT THE INSTANCE — all THREE degrade-to-warn arms**, or a later reader finds two of three fixed and infers the third was deliberate. **(2) THE METHOD IS PART OF THE ACT, AND GETTING IT WRONG PRODUCES A CONFIDENT-LOOKING REFUTATION OF A TRUE DEFECT.** BOB #11 needed three attempts: RENAMING the predicate dirties the tree, and `chmod 000` dirties it too (git reports a file modified when it cannot read it), so both make `plancheck` fail on UNPUBLISHED and exit 1 — which reads as *cannot reproduce*. **Only `--local`, which skips the publication half, isolates the variable.** Drive it that way or the confound masks the defect. **(3) `M-4` NAMES BOTH A MEASUREMENT ENTRY AND A QUEUE ITEM — two allocation spaces under one prefix — and that must be RESOLVED before an allocation site can be declared for `M`.** `mintid` flags it. **And the census answered this row's open question: `mintid` is not merely uncalled at a site — its OWN bypass detector (`--audit --base`) is itself `exists / optional / unauditable`, sitting in CONDUCT's loop and called by no gate.**

scope: **MAKE STALENESS RE-AFFIRMED RATHER THAN ACCUMULATED.** A `DELEGATION` block in `CLAIMS.md` carries no date except the one it was RAISED on, so a block that was true when written stays indistinguishable from one that is true now, forever and silently. The mechanism, and it is deliberately the cheapest one that cannot be satisfied by doing nothing: **every `DELEGATION` block carries EITHER a discharge line OR an explicit `open as of YYYY-MM-DD` line, and `plancheck` FAILS a block whose most recent of the two is older than a stated threshold.** That converts an unattended five-week drift into a line somebody must re-write, and it converts *the past stated as the present* into *the past stated as the past, with a date on it*. **Pick the threshold from the measured distribution rather than from taste, and say what you picked and why** — **the distribution must be RE-MEASURED and this row will not hand you a number, because the number this row was first written with was already false when it was written** — it said nine blocks spanning one day to five weeks, measured before the same session's sweep discharged the five-week tail; minutes later the honest reading was ten blocks all raised within one day. The five-week span was real and is the reason this row exists; it is also gone, and a row quoting it as present would be this row's own subject. **The FAIL is the point and a warn is not good enough**: this project already knows what a reported-not-gated arm is worth (VF-1's class), and a register nobody is forced to re-affirm is exactly a control that is DECLARED and never RUN.
accepts-when: a `DELEGATION` block with neither line FAILS `plancheck` by name, driven; a block with a fresh `open as of` PASSES and a block whose `open as of` is past the threshold FAILS, both driven; the nine blocks live on 2026-09-15 are each carried to a passing state by a real answer (a discharge where the tree already discharged it, an `open as of` where it is genuinely open) and NOT by a blanket date stamp — **a sweep that makes the instrument green without reading the tree is the defect this row exists to prevent, arriving one layer up**; `node tools/plancheck.mjs --local` 0 fail; `cd bio-plane && npm run test:battery` green own-baseline; `node scripts/coverage.mjs --strict` DIRECTLY, `$?` unpiped, exit 0; `node civicos-ui/test/run.mjs` from the repo root, unpiped, exit 0.

scope: **BOB'S RULING, 2026-09-17, VERBATIM:** *"NO_FALSIFIER is a condition that should be surfaced. But I think it should also be something a member can override either temporarily or in the published record."* **VERIFIED AT THE ARTIFACT BY CONDUCT #3 BEFORE ROWING, not inherited from the inbox entry:** `bio-plane/src/store.mjs:4792` returns `{ ok: false, reason: "NO_FALSIFIER" }` today, and `affordances.mjs:1093` records that the affordance is assigned BECAUSE the store refuses. **THIS IS CONSISTENT WITH DOCTRINE ALREADY HERE RATHER THAN A LOOSENING OF IT** — undetermined is first-class and must be STATED, and a gate that pressures someone into inventing a value is a bug in the gate. The shape is the one this record uses everywhere: the finding CONCLUDES, and carries *no falsifier stated* as a **first-class value that is never blank and never inferred**; the override **NAMES WHO AND WHEN**; and it is visible on **every surface the finding appears on, INCLUDING THE PUBLISHED RECORD**, because Bob named that case specifically. **A SILENT OVERRIDE IS THE ONLY WRONG ANSWER.** **THE DESIGN SENTENCE MUST MOVE WITH THE CODE:** the home document states the falsifier is REQUIRED, which Bob has now overruled — update it citing the ruling. **If you find the change is larger than bringing the document to Bob's ruling — if it reaches the claim object or the collapse — STOP and route it to BOB rather than widening**, because the item follows the design and not the other way round.
accepts-when: a finding with no falsifier CONCLUDES through `op=conclude`, **driven THROUGH THE OP and not at the store** (`op=invitelook` shipped with a ReferenceError while 1,276 assertions passed), and reads back carrying *no falsifier stated* as an explicit value with the overriding member and the time; **a finding that HAS a falsifier is byte-identical to today**; the override appears on the PUBLISHED surface and an assertion pins that, because the published case is where Bob said it must be visible; the affordance in `affordances.mjs` moves in step with the store rather than being left asserting a refusal that no longer happens; `cd bio-plane && npm run test:battery` green own-baseline; `node scripts/coverage.mjs --strict` DIRECTLY, `$?` unpiped, exit 0; `node civicos-ui/test/run.mjs` from the repo root, unpiped, exit 0; `node tools/plancheck.mjs --local`, then BARE after committing; `node tools/corpuscheck.mjs` green with the home document's front matter updated in the same commit.
NEGATIVE CONTROL: run and recorded — the override removed → the falsifier-less conclude REFUSES again and the suite FAILS BY NAME; **and the arm that matters more, because it is the one the ruling is about: an override that lands SILENTLY — no actor, no time, or absent from the published surface — must FAIL**, since a silent override is the only wrong answer and an arm that only checks the conclude succeeded would pass it. Over-strictness: a finding that HAS a falsifier must be unchanged in every answer, and **the condition must still be SURFACED** — Bob asked for it to be overridable, not invisible, so an implementation that stops mentioning the missing falsifier at all fails this row. **State how a liar would satisfy this before stating what it checks:** the cheapest green is to drop the refusal and store nothing — every conclude then succeeds, the suite goes quiet, and the record silently stops distinguishing a finding whose falsifier was stated from one whose absence a member accepted.

### REC-111 · done — landed `cc9e070c`, merged at `57ad571f` by CONDUCT #1, 2026-09-16. **A UNIT BUDGET — `CAPTURE_TEXT_CAPTURE_UNIT_BOUND` = 4,096 — chosen by MEASUREMENT (M-35) and not by preference**, tested in the SAME branch as the byte bound and counted into the same `over_bound`, so neither hides the other, which is §4.3's own ask. **CHUNKING WAS REFUSED ON EVIDENCE: neither route that reaches the index writer can produce a write that does not FIT a tick** — the acquire wire ceilings at 4,064 units (22.8% of the window) and a caller-authored `provenance.json` at 13,720 (40.9%) — and making chunking necessary would first require RAISING the wire's byte budget, **the exact regression §4.3 was corrected for the same day.** **THE ROW'S PREMISE WAS HALF WRONG AND THE CORRECTION IS WORTH MORE THAN THE BOUND:** *a container whose units are many and small is bounded by nothing this design specifies* is **true of the DESIGN and false of the SYSTEM** — both routes were already bounded and nothing was broken. **What was wrong is that BOTH BOUNDS WERE ACCIDENTS**: one falls out of a JSON envelope ESTIMATE, the other out of an inline-file limit that knows nothing about indexing, neither written down, either moving the day an unrelated constant moves. **A bound nobody can state without arithmetic across two files is not a decision about what a promote may cost — it is a side effect wearing one.** And M-20's 20,571-unit docx is not the counter-example it reads as: through the wire ~2,788 units are kept and it lands `partial` today, before and after — **a cost quoted for a document the wire never sends whole is a cost nothing pays.** **NO CHECK WAS ADDED AT THE WIRE AND THE ABSENCE IS MEASURED: the largest budget that regresses nothing (4,096) is ABOVE the most the wire can send (4,064), so a wire-side check PROVABLY CANNOT FIRE** — and a check that cannot fire is a mechanism believed on its existence; the ceiling is pinned by assertion instead. **ONE ARM CAME BACK DIFFERENT AND IS THE ITEM'S BEST FINDING: `tighten` was declared with eight failures and returned FIVE, because three assertions READ THE BOUND OUT OF THE PRODUCT so both sides move with it.** **An assertion written against the product's own constant can prove the MECHANISM right and can never prove the NUMBER right** — the costs-nothing-equality rule arriving in a new place, and why the four arms carrying INDEPENDENT figures all went red. The arm also produced the item's thesis as a control result: the worst-PDF arm survived a 512-unit bound only because the byte budget had already trimmed it to 411. **FL-10's guard fires on this change and the worker caught it before the gate did**, killing its stale-artifact battery BY PID from a process table filtered to its own worktree and **verifying a sibling worker's battery was still running and untouched** — never `pkill -f`, on a machine with five other live workers. Baseline CONFIRMED CONDUCT #1's exactly at 208/208 · 13,013 with 3/3 fleet members RAN. **NO IC OWED and the worker said why: the bound TRIMS and reports `partial`, it does not refuse, and no wire shape moves.** **Prior state, kept as the record: running, then queued.** Falsify rather than believe: a live worker holds an `agent-*` worktree with a claim on the paths its scope names; **if none does, this row is UNDETERMINED between `queued` and done-awaiting-integration — READ THE BRANCH (the preamble's falsification rule), and never conclude `queued` from the absence alone.** **Prior state, kept as the record: queued** — **THE UNIT-COUNT BOUND: a unit budget beside the byte budget AT THE SAME WIRE, so both are stated in one place and neither hides the other.** **Bytes do not bound the unit count, and the index costs ROWS and FTS ENTRIES.** M-20's ladder, read off rather than re-measured: the worst docx is **20,571 units at 1,187,253 B — INSIDE the byte bound — at 218 ms, 84.8% of the 257 ms window**, against §4.3's own *"45.7%, so the bound cannot by itself push a promote over the ceiling"*, which is true AT PAGE GRAIN ONLY. A container whose units are many and small is bounded by nothing this design specifies today. — waits on nothing; owner RECORD.

depends-on: CASE-1. **PARALLEL WITH CASE-2 BY DEPENDENCY AND CONTENDING WITH IT ON GROUND — see the sequencing note under the CASE heading.**
scope: **Design doc is the authority.** Version pinning: members frozen by version hash on the finding's existing version chain; an edit touching a published version mints a NEW version; **the pinned version is never mutated.**
accepts-when: as the design doc's CASE-3 bullet.
added: 2026-08-10 · CONDUCT
landed: `e8f6c85`/`0cb02cc`, merged on `main`. **CLAUSE 3 HAD TWO HALVES AND THEY WERE DIFFERENT SHAPES OF MISSING.** (1) **The pin was never written** — CASE-1 landed `published_case_members.version_sha` and NOTHING FILLED IT, so a published case named its members and froze nothing. `publish()` now writes it from the ratifying member's own signed `bundle_sha`, and **each member pins its OWN row at its OWN ratification**, because the roster is written by whichever member ratifies first, when the others have signed nothing — writing all N pins there would mean inventing N−1. (2) **The door that moves a finding's claims was standing open**: `#moveVersionState` had no published-state guard while BOTH its neighbours already refused exactly this, and `PUBLISHED_CANNOT_RESTRUCTURE`'s wording describes the version door precisely. New `PUBLISHED_CANNOT_MOVE_VERSION` (C-25.34) in the EXISTING `VERSION_ACT_CHECKS` — no new family, avoiding C-22's floor tax. **The fence is `to !== null` and that line is the CATALOG'S OWN (`VERSION_ACT_TO`), not the worker's judgement**: `hide` (a prune D-214 rules never deletes) and `current` (a project's stance) stay outside. **NO SCHEMA CHANGE AT ALL**, which also removed any collision risk with CASE-2. **THE PROOF IS DRIVEN THROUGH THE ANONYMOUS OP:** publish edition 1, reopen the finding, move the reading (now permitted), republish as edition 2, then re-read EDITION 1 through `op=publishedcase` and assert its `version_sha`, `bundle_sha`, `sig_armored` and `ratified_at` are unchanged and that its pin names edition 1's hash and NOT edition 2's — with the expected hash taken from the sha fed to `ssh-keygen -Y sign` BEFORE ratification, so the two sides of every pin assertion share no code path. Battery 165/165 → **166/166 · 10,193**; `--strict` exit 0 read unpiped. NCs 7 arms armed ALONE. **ARM (f) EXISTS BECAUSE ARM (b) MEASURED SOMETHING OTHER THAN WHAT IT WAS WRITTEN TO MEASURE, AND BOTH ARE KEPT** — removing the write-once predicate reddened only the STRUCTURAL assertion, and the reason is a fact about the plane rather than about the arm: the pin UPDATE is keyed `(case_id, EDITION, bundle_id)`, so a later edition writes a later edition's row and can NEVER reach edition 1's, and `EDITION_EXISTS` refuses a second sha long before the pin write. **The predicate is genuinely unreachable — claimed in words at the site and now MEASURED rather than argued** — so (f) mutates the pin by the route that IS reachable and fails exactly the two assertions saying the pin did not move. Over-strictness arm (d) widened the fence to all six acts and went red, keeping `hide` and `current` outside. **Two superseded assertions CORRECTED, never exempted** — CASE-1's `version_sha is NULL` (now the pin) and `versionstate`'s registry-equality floor, which caught the new code immediately and was working as designed; CASE-1's control driver re-run, all five arms still red. UI floors moved with **1/3/1/2 of the movement measured as PRE-EXISTING SLACK rather than this item's**, established by reverting `bio-checks.mjs` to HEAD. **HANDED TO CASE-5, and it is the pin's whole point: resolving a member BY THE PIN instead of by the case's edition number is NOT done.** Today `version_sha` and the served `bundle_sha` agree only because a member's edition is still slaved to its case's; **CASE-5 is where they can diverge and where the pin starts doing work no other column can.**

### CASE-4 · done
milestone: M10
interface: I3/I5; State Rules amendment
depends-on: CASE-2, CASE-3
scope: **Design doc is the authority.** Lifecycle and the revision flag: `published` REMOVED from the inquiry state machine; containing cases FLAGGED when a member finding revises; **flags set-but-never-clear until each owning project acts.** The precondition survives as *only a CONCLUDED finding may be a case member*.
accepts-when: as the design doc's CASE-4 bullet.
added: 2026-08-10 · CONDUCT
landed: `3f6b886`, merged on `main`. **THE PRECONDITION AND THE STATE WERE ONE ARRAY ENTRY CARRYING TWO RULES, and that is the whole item.** `concluded -> published` said BOTH *publication moves the state* (which DEC-72 deletes) and *publication is reachable from `concluded` and nowhere else* (which DEC-72 does NOT). **Delete the entry and `legalFrom.includes("published")` is false from EVERY state — a gate that reads as refusing everything and has in fact stopped asking.** `publishCase()` now carries `NOT_CONCLUDED` as its own named refusal, and block 2 proves both halves in one place: the edge is gone from the catalog's own table AND an open inquiry is still refused, by name, through `op=publish`. **FOUR MORE RULES RODE ON THAT SAME TABLE AND WOULD HAVE DIED SILENTLY — every one found by RUNNING the suites, not by reading:** `op=dispose` let a published case become deferrable (**D-79 reversed by a lifecycle change**, now `PUBLISHED_CANNOT_BE_SET_DOWN`); `op=publish` accepted a second edition of bytes nobody revised, and **C-21.1 did NOT catch it because it only compares against a RATIFIED prior** (now `ALREADY_A_CASE_MEMBER`); `inquirydivide`'s affordance was offered where the op refuses (DEC-8); and `checkCompletenessFreshness` would have returned on every document, **letting an edition reprint the last one's limits with the catalog silent.** **THE PIN DIVERGENCE IS REUSED AND NO SECOND MECHANISM WAS BUILT:** `#caseRelationOf` asks CASE-5's own question from the member's side — is this finding's CURRENT `bundle_sha` the `version_sha` some roster froze? — so **the relation and the flag are ONE comparison over ONE column read two ways**, and a marker in the bytes would have been a second authority for a fact the pin already holds. The flag is raised in `promote()`, the one write that mints a version, so every revision route is caught at one call site. **A LIMIT MEASURED AND STATED RATHER THAN PAPERED OVER: a case with several owning projects is NOT REPRESENTABLE** — `cases` is keyed on `case_id` alone (CASE-1) and `FINDING_IN_ANOTHER_CASE` still refuses a finding into a second case — so block 7 proves the scoping on the shape the store CAN build (two cases, two owning projects, one project acting) and the suite says plainly that this is the measurable shape, not the one the brief described. NCs 7 arms + baseline, each armed ALONE. **TWO CAME BACK NOT AS DECLARED AND BOTH CORRECTIONS ARE THE USEFUL HALF:** (b2) ran GREEN first time because of the FIXTURE'S ORDERING rather than the plane — the second project revised AFTER the first acted, so an unscoped discharge had nothing to over-reach; **an instrument limit, and the THIRD of that exact shape after CASE-3's (f) and CASE-5's (c)**. And (d) killed the fixture and produced NO TALLY AT ALL, **because a bare `throw` names nothing** — the fixture now reports through `bail()` and (d2) was added beside it to reach the over-strictness question (d) never gets to. **IC-69 filed before any code; impact NOT zero** — `civicos-ui/` held a HAND COPY of the machine this item changed, and its own harness caught it. **THE WORKER DID SOMETHING ITS CLAIM SAID IT WOULD NOT, AND REPORTED IT PLAINLY:** the UI harness went red and a delegation cannot carry a red gate, so it corrected three mirror sites and recorded a CLAIMS amendment — **and its FIRST correction was WRONG** (deleting `PHASE.published` turned three more suites red, and they were right: the UI is a READER of bytes already signed), reverted whole and replaced. **CASE-5b's wall was NOT walked into:** nothing here commits a case fact from an unsigned request — the flag is two hashes this plane already holds, compared, and the discharge is a RATIFIED edition, an act that already exists and is already signed. It deliberately did not mint an acknowledgement op, which would have been exactly that attribution class.

### CASE-5 · done — **PARTIAL BY DESIGN; the remaining half is CASE-5b below, and this row names it rather than absorbing it**
milestone: M10
interface: I3 via the IC protocol
depends-on: CASE-2, CASE-3
scope: **Design doc is the authority.** The artifact flip: case-side freezing; **finding bytes stop naming a case**; `op=verify` / `op=publishedcase` / `op=publishedmanifest` read the case artifact; **the stranger-verification path proven END TO END** — that property is REC-44's and must be preserved case-side, not dropped with it; checks corrected never exempted.
accepts-when: as the design doc's CASE-5 bullet; a stranger holding published material verifies WITHOUT contacting the instance, driven.
added: 2026-08-10 · CONDUCT
landed: `e3cbc94`, merged on `main`. **THE MEMBER'S EDITION IS UNSLAVED FROM THE CASE'S, and the item's first act was to MEASURE that they could not diverge on any path.** `op=publish` stamped the case's edition into every member and `op=ratify` committed it, so a member's edition WAS its case's by construction — **which is what "one case per finding baked into the FORMAT" actually meant: a finding published at edition 1 could not join a second case, because that case's edition 1 demanded bytes at a number the finding had already spent, and `EDITION_EXISTS` refused it.** So the flip is a FORMAT change first and the pin resolution is what it enables. Each member now stamps its OWN next edition off its own published chain, with the case's number travelling beside it as `case_edition:`, both inside the signed bytes and both read at ratification out of the signed document and nothing else. `#caseEditionState` resolves a member BY ITS PIN (`bundle_sha = version_sha`), with the old case-edition predicate surviving ONLY as the honest fallback for a pre-CASE-3 roster row whose pin is NULL. **FOUR MORE SITES CARRIED THE SAME CONFLATION THROUGH AN ARGUMENT LIST RATHER THAN A WHERE CLAUSE** — found by asking which callers of `#caseOf(bundleId, edition)` held a `published_bundles` row — and **`publishedEditions` was the worst: a finding at its own edition 1 inside a case at edition 3 was answered with EDITION 1's scope, completeness and bias acknowledgement.** Case-side freezing: `published_cases` gains `bar` as an additive COLUMN (no new table, so `purge` is untouched and D-113 does not bite), committed from the signed bytes under the existing `CASE_ASSERTION_DIVERGED` refusal. Container to `bio-case-container/4`, and **it had been writing the CASE's edition number onto every member — a false statement in the one artifact nobody can check against us**; `findings[].signature.statement` was a `Uint8Array` that `JSON.stringify` rendered as an object of byte indices, so the artifact told a stranger to verify over a statement printed as 47 numbered integers (zero consumers measured; corrected to ASCII). **THE STRANGER DRIVE IS REAL RATHER THAN NOMINAL: phase B REPLACES `mf.dispatchFetch` WITH A THROW** — the instance is unreachable, not merely uncalled — and every signature verifies under `ssh-keygen -Y verify` against the key the artifact names, over a statement rebuilt from the artifact's own id and hash; **one flipped byte fails all three checks while the untouched copy still passes, so the verification is not vacuous.** Battery 167/167 → **168/168 · 10,334** on its branch; `--strict` exit 0 unpiped; UI harness exit 0. NCs 6 arms + baseline, each armed ALONE. **ONE ARM CAME BACK NOT AS DECLARED AND THE CORRECTION IS WORTH MORE THAN THE ARM:** the over-strictness arm was "require a pin on every roster row", predicted RED and ran GREEN — **because this fixture writes no unpinned row. That is an INSTRUMENT LIMIT, not a defence that held**, and it is kept as arm (f) carrying that measurement while (c) was rewritten as the over-strictness question this fixture can actually answer. Arms (a) and (c) fail on the SAME 22 assertions, **verified by DIFFING THE FAILURE SETS rather than inferred from equal tallies** — different causes, one effect. Blind-by-construction avoided three ways: pins taken from the pre-ratification signing sha, block 6 parsed out of the design doc at run time (looked for in `docs/development/` AND `docs/archive/`, because CASE-6 archives it), and signatures checked by an external binary sharing no code path with `src/`. **IC-66 filed BEFORE any code with impact that is NOT zero** — one file, one function, three lines: `civicos-ui/app.html`'s `pubIndex` joins a roster row on the CASE's edition while `byId` is keyed on the finding's own, so **a diverged member MISSES SILENTLY — awaiting ratification forever, blank pair, blank bar, and listed a second time as in no case.** Enqueued as **UI-56**. Three superseded assertions corrected with dated reasons; `publishedcase`'s UI-35 arm corrected by NAMING `bar`/`bar_detail` as unread with reasons and pointing at CASE-6, never exempted.
**WHAT THIS ROW DID NOT DO, AND WHY IT IS NOT A SHORTFALL: FINDING BYTES STILL NAME A CASE.** `case_id`, `case_findings`, `case_roles`, `case_scope`, `bias_acknowledgement` and `required_strength` remain stamped in every member. The half that was load-bearing ON THE FORMAT — the edition conflation — is removed; the rest stopped at a doctrinal wall that is MEASURED rather than judged. **Every case fact this plane commits is committed from the SIGNED BYTES and from nothing else** (`#publishEdges`' doctrine, restated at seven sites in `publish()`), **and there is no signature over a case for those facts to move to** — the container manifest says so in its own words: *a case-level signature would be a signature over something nobody reviewed.* Removing them without first minting a case-level signing ceremony would leave the plane committing a group's case assertions **from an UNSIGNED REQUEST**, which is the attribution class this record refuses everywhere else. **`caseflip.test.mjs` ASSERTS THAT THE BYTES STILL CARRY THOSE KEYS, so "still there" is distinguishable from "nobody checked"** — which is the difference between a stated limit and a silent one. Multi-case membership stays REFUSED and the refusal is DRIVEN, so its state is pinned: the flip makes it representable, and lifting the fence is a surface question that belongs with CASE-6.

milestone: M7
interface: I4 + I6 — **IC-70 is PRE-MINTED for it**, so FLEET does not mint an id in a worktree that cannot see a parallel worker's file (the IC-64 lesson: on 2026-08-10 two parallel workers each minted `IC-64` because `mintid` reads its floor from ids mentioned in PROSE, and each was RIGHT about the corpus it could read)
depends-on: FL-9 (landed). **D-298's RELEASE half is DIST's and waits on this; the format/installer half does not.**
scope: **D-298 — DIST measured the MIRROR of FL-9's defect: the plane's committed bundle is 114 COMMITS STALE against `src`, and the battery cannot tell.** The reason generalises and is why this is worth an item: **the battery proves the artifact WORKS, never that it MATCHES its source.** A suite that boots a stale bundle and gets correct answers is reporting on a build nobody ships from. Extend FL-9's guard to `bio-plane`'s own bundle: byte-identity with a fresh build, the prove-it-can-fail arm, **a stale artifact FAILS instead of shipping.** Routed to FLEET under the standing delegation as a SCOPING call rather than doctrine — **the guard discipline is FLEET's wherever a committed bundle exists, the plane's included.**
**REUSE FL-9's LIBRARY, DO NOT WRITE A SECOND ONE** (`bio-plane/scripts/fleet-bundle.mjs` is one expression of the recipe and one of the check). **AND CARRY ITS TWO MEASURED SURPRISES, because neither is obvious and both cost the first worker real time:** (1) **`esbuild` writes input paths relative to the process cwd** — identical source built from two directories differed by **30 bytes**, a FALSE STALE; pin `absWorkingDir` and record it. (2) **`esbuild` TREE-SHAKES an unused export out of a non-entry module, so byte-identity ALONE passed a real committed-source change** — comment-only edits are invisible to it too — **so the dependency-free INPUT-HASH arm is load-bearing and not a fallback.** A plane-bundle guard built on byte-identity alone would repeat a defect this estate has already measured and written down.
claim: **PRECISELY, and this is not boilerplate — a CASE-4 worker may still be live on RECORD's ground.** Name the guard suite and the build script; **NEVER `store.mjs` or `schema.mjs`.** If the work seems to need them, that is a finding to report, not a path to claim.

NEGATIVE CONTROL: run and recorded, armed ALONE — (1) **the arm this item exists for**: edit `bio-plane/src` without rebuilding and the gate must FAIL naming it; (2) **the tree-shake arm** — remove an unused export from a NON-ENTRY module, which byte-identity alone will MISS, and the input-hash arm must still fail; (3) over-strictness — a legitimately rebuilt byte-identical bundle must still pass, and a docs-only change must not fail the build.
added: 2026-09-10 · CONDUCT (draining the 2026-09-10 BOB INBOX entry as an ITEM. **Minted rather than deferred to CONDUCT #9**: the entry said either was fine and losing it was not, and a mint is a bounded act while a handoff note is a promise. **Not spawned** — FLEET is a standing area session now and this is its ground.)
